name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: Tanker attacks near Hormuz on 29–30 Oct; Red Sea route still contested
state: Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after striking mines near Hormuz on 31 Oct, and Iran reported four such fires that day; Oman rescued 25 crew from a burning vessel on 30 Oct. Ship attacks near the strait hit a record in October. Iran's terms for reopening, discussed in Doha on 31 Oct, include sanctions relief and recognition of its routes.
for_you: Disrupted shipping lanes raise fuel and goods prices and lengthen delivery times. FCDO advice applies for travel to the Gulf region.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.
